issuing_body: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
title: Minnesota Could Better Ensure That Childcare Assistance Providers Comply With Attendance Requirements
findings: For 38 of 200 randomly selected childcare assistance payments, Minnesota did not comply with attendance/payment requirements; OIG found no attendance/payment errors in the other 162 sampled payments.
OIG estimated that 11 percent of payments made to 1,155 licensed childcare centers in 2023 had one or more attendance/payment errors.
OIG concluded Minnesota's limited oversight of attendance documentation resulted in overpayments to providers.
recommendations: Work with childcare providers to collect, as appropriate, overpayments identified by the audit.
Strengthen monitoring to include routine reviews of CCAP attendance records for accuracy.
Continue steps toward real-time electronic childcare attendance reporting, as Minnesota OLA had previously recommended.

recommendation_status_as_of_2026_08_14.notes: Tracker was last updated 2026-08-14 and still displayed all three recommendations as Open Unimplemented.

source_locators.audit_highlights: one-page HHS-OIG Report Highlights; screenshot captured 2026-08-29

does_not_support: The 11 percent estimate is an attendance/payment error rate, not a fraud rate.
The audit does not say 11 percent of CCAP payments were stolen.
An attendance-documentation error may have multiple causes; the audit does not establish criminal intent for every error.
The report does not provide a statewide criminal-fraud loss total.
Open-unimplemented recommendation status is an implementation-status record, not proof that no corrective activity has occurred; Minnesota had concurred and described planned/actions taken.
